title: Expositio totius mundi et gentium (Description of the Whole World and Its Peoples) / RU: «Описание всего мира и народов»
author: Anonymous (Greek original, possibly by a Syrian merchant); anonymous Latin translators
date: Greek original 350–362 CE; surviving Latin versions 6th c.
size: 67 chapters; est. 6–7k words; two Latin versions
edition: Rougé, Sources Chrétiennes 124 (1966); Cioffi, Teubner (De Gruyter 2025). Public-domain Riese, Geographi Latini Minores 1878: https://archive.org/details/geographilatinim00ries
ru_evidence: No ru.wikipedia article (404). Absent from the ancientrome, vostlit and simposium catalogues. No Russian translation found.
en_evidence: Only J. Woodman's 1964 Ohio State MA thesis, available online. en.wikipedia: a widely available printed English translation 'has never been published'.
other_translations: French: Rougé 1966. No Italian or German translation found.
value: A unique mid-4th-c. panorama of the empire's trade goods, cities, shows and peoples (Antioch, Alexandria, Persia), and important for vulgar Latin. Short, self-contained, with a new 2025 critical text: an ideal pilot.
ai_feasibility: medium–high: short text but vulgar, corrupt Latin. The two versions check each other; the commentary must handle commodities and place names.
pilot_unit: Entire text, both Latin versions in parallel (67 chapters, est. 6–7k words)
